## 2. troubleshooting
URL: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/troubleshooting

issues and how to fix them

## Installation Issues

 
 
 If the install script fails to download:

 1. Check your internet connection
 2. Verify curl is installed: `which curl`
 3. Try with verbose output: `curl -fsSL -v https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash`

 If you're behind a corporate proxy, you may need to configure proxy settings:

    ```bash theme={null}
    export https_proxy=http://your-proxy:port
    curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash
    ```
 

 
 If the PowerShell install script fails:

 1. Check your internet connection
 2. Ensure you are running PowerShell as a regular user (not as Administrator unless necessary)
 3. If you see an execution policy error, try:
       ```powershell theme={null}
       Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
       irm https://static.devin.ai/cli/setup.ps1 | iex
       ```
 4. If you're behind a corporate proxy, configure proxy settings in PowerShell before running the install command

 As an alternative to the PowerShell script, you can download and run the standalone installer directly:

 * [x86\_64](https://static.devin.ai/cli/devin-updater-x86_64-pc-windows.exe)
 * [ARM64](https://static.devin.ai/cli/devin-updater-aarch64-pc-windows.exe)
 

 
 The installer needs write access to install the binary. If you see permission errors:

 1. Check the install location has write permissions
 2. Do not run the installer with `sudo` â€” this can cause ownership issues
 3. If installing to a system directory, ensure your user has appropriate permissions
 

 
 If the install completes but `devin` isn't found:

 **macOS / Linux / WSL:**

 1. Restart your terminal or run `source ~/.bashrc` (or `~/.zshrc`)
 2. Check if the binary location is in your PATH: `echo $PATH`
 3. Verify the binary exists: `ls -la ~/.local/bin/devin` (or the install location shown during setup)

 **Windows:**

 1. Restart your PowerShell session
 2. Check if the binary location is in your PATH: `$env:PATH -split ';'...

## 3. stable
URL: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable

* Long conversations are compacted earlier in the background so the agent spends less time pausing when context is nearly full.
 * ATIF exports now include richer per-step transcript details, including telemetry and timing metrics.
 * Shell commands that continue running in the background after a timeout now report how long Devin waited before returning.
 * The built-in Explore subagent can now use web search to research topics outside the codebase, in addition to its read-only codebase tools. It still cannot fetch arbitrary URLs or edit files.

## 4. revanthpobala/devin-cli
URL: https://github.com/revanthpobala/devin-cli

For external automation and AI agent architectures relying on the CLI, `devin-cli` supports a global `--json` flag. This will suppress all visual output/terminal colors and instead uniformly return raw JSON objects for stdout and API errors, making the CLI completely deterministic to parse.
...
Profiles are stored in `~/.config/devin/config.json` â€” fully isolated including session caches and active session IDs.

## 3. global-vs-local
URL: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/configuration/global-vs-local

Devin CLI loads configuration from multiple sources and merges them together. Understanding the precedence order helps you set up the right configuration for your team and personal preferences.
...
| Priority | Source | Notes |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| 1 (highest) | Organization / Team Settings | Cannot be overridden |
| 2 | Session (interactive approvals) | In-memory only |
| 3 | Project Local (`.devin/config.local.json`) | Personal, gitignored |
| 4 | Project (`.devin/config.json`) | Shared with team |
| 5 (lowest) | User (`~/.config/devin/config.json`; `%APPDATA%\devin\config.json` on Windows) | Your defaults |
...
## When to Use Each Level

 
 
 **Path:** `~/.config/devin/config.json` (`%APPDATA%\devin\config.json` on Windows)

 Use for personal preferences that apply everywhere:

 * Default model preference
 * Theme preference
 * Personal MCP servers (e.g., your own API keys)
 * Global permission grants

    ```json theme={null}
    {
      "agent": { "model": "opus" },
      "permissions": {
        "allow": ["Read(**)", "Exec(git)"]
      }
    }
    ```
 

 
 **Path:** `.devin/config.json`

 Use for team standards committed to the repository. Only `permissions`, `mcpServers`, `read_config_from`, and `hooks` are available at this level:

 * Shared MCP servers (with non-secret config)
 * Team permission policies
 * Import settings
 * Lifecycle hooks

    ```json theme={null}
    {
      "permissions": {
        "allow": ["Exec(npm run)", "Read(src/**)"],
        "deny": ["Exec(sudo)"]
      },
      "mcpServers": {
        "github": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 

 
 **Path:** `.devin/config.local.json`

 Use for personal overrides that shouldn't be committed:

 * API keys and secrets
 * Personal tool preferences for this project
 * Permission overrides

    ```json the...

- Tool names come directly from `tool_calls[].function_name`; the provider assumes valid ATIF tool-call records.

## 5. 
URL: https://docs.devinenterprise.com/cli/extensibility/configuration

> How to configure Devin CLI behavior with config files
...
Devin CLI is configured through JSON files (with comment support) at the user and project level. These config files control the agent's model, permissions, MCP servers, and more.
...
Path: `~/.config/devin/config.json`
...
Your personal defaults that apply across all projects. This is where you set your preferred model, theme, and global permissions.
...
## Project config
...
Path: `.devin/config.json` (at your project root)
...
Shared team configuration committed to version control. Use this for project-specific MCP servers, permission policies, and import settings.
...
Path: `.devin/config.local.json`
...
Personal overrides for this project that aren't committed to git (automatically gitignored). Use this for secrets, API keys, and personal preference overrides.
...
The fastest way to get started is to create a `.devin/config.json` in your project root:
...
You can also configure Devin CLI interactively: when the agent asks for permission, choose to save the decision to your project or user config for next time.
...
## Project vs User Settings
...
Not all settings are available at every level. Project configs (`.devin/config.json` and `.devin/config.local.json`) support:
...
- `permissions` â€” allow, deny, and ask rules
- `mcpServers` â€” MCP server definitions
- `read_config_from` â€” import settings from Cursor, Windsurf, and Claude
- `hooks` â€” lifecycle hooks (see Hooks)
...
All other settings â€” including `agent` (model), `theme_mode`, `unicode_mode`, `show_path`, `sandbox`, and other display/behavior options â€” are user-config only and can only be set in the user config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`; `%APPDATA%\devin\config.json` on Windows).

def write_thinking_file(session_id: str, agent_responses: list) -> None:
    """Write agent responses to a separate thinking file, sorted by timestamp."""
    log_dir = Path("Logs/Architect/Session")
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Find existing session file to match naming convention
    session_name = session_id.title() if session_id else "Unknown"
    md_files = list(log_dir.glob(f"Architect_*_{session_name}.md"))
    
    if not md_files:
        print(f"WARNING: No session log file found for: {session_name}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available files in {log_dir}:", file=sys.stderr)
        for file in log_dir.glob("*.md"):
            print(f"  - {file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    # Use the most recent session file to get the naming pattern
    session_file = max(md_files, key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime)
    print(f"Found session file: {session_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Create thinking file with matching naming convention (avoid double "Thinking")
    if "Architect_Thinking_" in session_file.name:
        # File already has Thinking prefix, use it as-is
        thinking_file = session_file
    else:
        # Replace only the first occurrence to avoid duplication
        thinking_file = session_file.parent / session_file.name.replace("Architect_", "Architect_Thinking_", 1)
    
    print(f"Creating thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Sort agent responses by timestamp
    sorted_responses = sorted(agent_responses, key=lambda x: x.get('timestamp', ''))
    
    try:
        # Write thinking file with header (overwrites existing)
        with open(thinking_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f"# Agent Thinking - {session_name}\n")
            f.write(f"**Session ID**: {session_id}\n")
            f.write(f"**Generated**: {datetime.now().isoformat()}\n")
            f.write(f"**Total Responses**: {len(sorted_responses)}\n")
            f.write("---\n\n")
            
            for response in sorted_responses:
                f.write(format_agent_response(response))
        
        print(f"Successfully created thinking file: {thinking_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to write thinking file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)

"""Minimal SessionEnd test - just writes to a file."""

import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    """Minimal SessionEnd test."""
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
        session_id = data.get("session_id", "unknown")
        reason = data.get("reason", "unknown")
        
        # Write to test file
        log_dir = Path("Logs/Architect/Session")
        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        test_file = log_dir / "session_end_minimal_test.txt"
        
        with open(test_file, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f"SessionEnd fired: {datetime.now().isoformat()}\n")
            f.write(f"Session ID: {session_id}\n")
            f.write(f"Reason: {reason}\n")
            f.write(f"---\n")
        
        print(f"SessionEnd test: SUCCESS - {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"SessionEnd test: ERROR - {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## 2. overview
URL: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview

Hooks are configured with a JSON format. Place them in your project's `.devin/` directory (or a user-level config) and Devin CLI runs them at the matching lifecycle events. Existing hooks in `.claude/` directories are also picked up automatically â€” see [Where Hooks Live](#where-hooks-live).
...
Create `.devin/hooks.v1.json` in your project:
...
```json theme={null}
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/check-command.sh"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
...
| Event | When it fires |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool finishes |
| `PermissionRequest` | When a permission decision is needed |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | When the user submits a message |
| `Stop` | When the agent wants to stop |
| `SessionStart` | When a session begins |
| `SessionEnd` | When a session ends |
...
Each hook has a **type** (`command` or `prompt`), an optional **matcher** (regex on the hook event's `tool_name`), and configuration:
...
```json theme={null}
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/validate.sh",
          "timeout": 10
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
...
| Field | Description |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `matcher` | Regex matched against the hook event's `tool_name`. Empty string or an omitted matcher matches all tool names. |
| `type` | `"command"` to run a shell command, or `"prompt"` to evaluate an LLM prompt. |
| `command` | Shell command to run (for `command` type). |
| `prompt` | LLM prompt to evaluate (for `prompt` type). |
| `timeout` | Timeout in seconds (optional). |
...
Command hooks run a shell command. Event data is passed as JSON on **stdin**, and the command can return JSON...

...
Devin CLI can read configuration from other AI coding tools you may already use:
...
| Source | What's Imported |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENTS.md` / `AGENT.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Rules (always-on context) |
| `.cursor/rules/*.md` / `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | Rules |
| `.windsurf/rules/*.md` | Rules |
| `.claude/` directory | Commands, [custom subagents](/cli/subagents#custom-subagents), [hooks](/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview) |
...
This means you can start using Devin CLI without rewriting your existing configuration. Import is enabled by default and can be controlled in your config file:
...
```json theme={null}
{
  "read_config_from": {
    "cursor": true,
    "windsurf": true,
    "claude": true
  }
}
```
...
Set any provider to `false` to disable importing from it.

## 5. 
URL: https://docs.devinenterprise.com/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview

Hooks are configured with a JSON format. Place them in your project's `.devin/` directory (or a user-level config) and Devin CLI runs them at the matching lifecycle events. Existing hooks in `.claude/` directories are also picked up automatically â€” see Where Hooks Live.
...
Create `.devin/hooks.v1.json` in your project:
...
```json
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/check-command.sh"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
...
| Event | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool finishes |
| `PermissionRequest` | When a permission decision is needed |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | When the user submits a message |
| `Stop` | When the agent wants to stop |
| `SessionStart` | When a session begins |
| `SessionEnd` | When a session ends |
...
## Hook Format
...
Each hook has a type (`command` or `prompt`), an optional matcher (regex on the hook event's `tool_name`), and configuration:
...
```json
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/validate.sh",
          "timeout": 10
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

```
...
| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `matcher` | Regex matched against the hook event's `tool_name`. Empty string or an omitted matcher matches all tool names. |
| `type` | `"command"` to run a shell command, or `"prompt"` to evaluate an LLM prompt. |
| `command` | Shell command to run (for `command` type). |
| `prompt` | LLM prompt to evaluate (for `prompt` type). |
| `timeout` | Timeout in seconds (optional). |
...
Command hooks run a shell command. Event data is passed as JSON on stdin, and the command can return JSON on stdout to control the outcome (see Output format below).
...
```json
{
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "exec",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "rm -rf /"
  },
  "session_id": "3f...

```

"""Agent response extractor - extracts agent text responses from transcript files."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


def format_agent_response(entry: dict) -> str:
    """Format an agent response entry for logging."""
    timestamp = entry.get('timestamp', '')
    reasoning = entry.get('reasoning_content', '')
    message = entry.get('message', '')
    model = entry.get('model_name', 'unknown')
    step_id = entry.get('step_id', 'unknown')
    
    formatted = []
    formatted.append("### AGENT_RESPONSE")
    formatted.append(f"**Timestamp**: {timestamp}")
    formatted.append(f"**Step ID**: {step_id}")
    formatted.append(f"**Model**: {model}")
    formatted.append("")
    
    # Combine reasoning and message for complete response
    full_response = ""
    if reasoning:
        full_response += reasoning
    if message:
        if full_response:
            full_response += "\n\n" + message
        else:
            full_response = message
    
    if full_response:
        formatted.append("**Response**:")
        formatted.append("```")
        formatted.append(full_response)
        formatted.append("```")
    else:
        formatted.append("**Response**: [empty]")
    
    formatted.append("---")
    formatted.append("")
    
    return "\n".join(formatted)


def extract_agent_responses(transcript_path: Path) -> list:
    """Extract agent responses from transcript file, filtering for meaningful thinking only."""
    try:
        with open(transcript_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            transcript = json.load(f)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to parse transcript: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return []
    
    agent_responses = []
    
    # Extract from steps array (ATIF-v1.7 format)
    steps = transcript.get('steps', [])
    for step in steps:
        # STRICT: Only include agent steps with source='agent'
        if step.get('source') != 'agent':
            continue
        
        # Skip if this is a tool call response (not actual thinking)
        if 'tool_calls' in step:
            continue
        
        reasoning = step.get('reasoning_content', '').strip()
        message = step.get('message', '').strip()
        
        # Skip steps without meaningful content
        if not reasoning and not message:
            continue
        
        # Filter out meta-commentary about the tool/script development
        meta_keywords = [
            'script', 'hook', 'extractor', 'formatting', 'markdown',
            'file structure', 'syntax highlighting', 'blue', 'plain text',
            'line 1058', 'before line', 'from line', 'AGENTS.md'
        ]
        
        # Check if content is mostly meta-commentary
        combined_content = (reasoning + ' ' + message).lower()
        if any(keyword in combined_content for keyword in meta_keywords):
            # Only include if it also contains substantive content
            substantive_keywords = ['user', 'task', 'work', 'fix', 'solve', 'implement', 'create', 'need']
            if not any(keyword in combined_content for keyword in substantive_keywords):
                continue
        
        agent_responses.append(step)
    
    print(f"Found {len(agent_responses)} meaningful agent responses", file=sys.stderr)
    
    return agent_responses


def write_thinking_file(session_id: str, agent_responses: list) -> None:
    """Write agent responses to a separate thinking file, sorted by timestamp."""
    log_dir = Path("Logs/Architect/Session")
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Find existing session file to match naming convention
    session_name = session_id.title() if session_id else "Unknown"
    md_files = list(log_dir.glob(f"Architect_*_{session_name}.md"))
    
    if not md_files:
        print(f"WARNING: No session log file found for: {session_name}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available files in {log_dir}:", file=sys.stderr)
        for file in log_dir.glob("*.md"):
            print(f"  - {file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    # Use the most recent session file to get the naming pattern
    session_file = max(md_files, key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime)
    print(f"Found session file: {session_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Create thinking file with matching naming convention (avoid double "Thinking")
    if "Architect_Thinking_" in session_file.name:
        # File already has Thinking prefix, use it as-is
        thinking_file = session_file
    else:
        # Replace only the first occurrence to avoid duplication
        thinking_file = session_file.parent / session_file.name.replace("Architect_", "Architect_Thinking_", 1)
    
    print(f"Target thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Delete existing thinking file if it exists
    if thinking_file.exists():
        print(f"Deleting existing thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        thinking_file.unlink()
    
    # Sort agent responses by timestamp
    sorted_responses = sorted(agent_responses, key=lambda x: x.get('timestamp', ''))
    
    try:
        # Create new thinking file with header
        with open(thinking_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f"# Agent Thinking - {session_name}\n")
            f.write(f"**Session ID**: {session_id}\n")
            f.write(f"**Generated**: {datetime.now().isoformat()}\n")
            f.write(f"**Total Responses**: {len(sorted_responses)}\n")
            f.write("---\n\n")
            
            for response in sorted_responses:
                f.write(format_agent_response(response))
        
        print(f"Successfully created thinking file: {thinking_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to write thinking file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)


def main() -> None:
    """Main function to extract and log agent responses."""
    print("Agent response extractor started", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Read session_id from stdin hook data
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
        print(f"Received hook data: {list(data.keys())}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to parse stdin JSON: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    session_id = data.get("session_id", "unknown")
    print(f"Session ID: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Find transcript file
    transcript_dir = Path(os.path.expandvars("%APPDATA%\\devin\\cli\\transcripts"))
    transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
    print(f"Looking for transcript: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Fallback to Linux/Mac path
    if not transcript_file.exists():
        transcript_dir = Path.home() / ".local/share/devin/cli/transcripts"
        transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        print(f"Fallback path: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    if not transcript_file.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: Transcript file not found: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available transcripts:", file=sys.stderr)
        try:
            for file in transcript_dir.glob("*.json"):
                print(f"  - {file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        except:
            pass
        return
    
    print(f"Extracting agent responses from transcript: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Extract agent responses
    agent_responses = extract_agent_responses(transcript_file)
    
    if not agent_responses:
        print(f"No agent responses found in transcript", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    print(f"Found {len(agent_responses)} agent responses", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Write to separate thinking file
    write_thinking_file(session_id, agent_responses)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        combined_content = (reasoning + ' ' + message).lower()
        if any(keyword in combined_content for keyword in meta_keywords):
            # Only include if it also contains substantive content
            substantive_keywords = ['user', 'task', 'work', 'fix', 'solve', 'implement', 'create', 'need']
            if not any(keyword in combined_content for keyword in substantive_keywords):
                continue
        
        agent_responses.append(step)
    
    print(f"Found {len(agent_responses)} meaningful agent responses", file=sys.stderr)
    
    return agent_responses


def write_thinking_file(session_id: str, agent_responses: list) -> None:
    """Write agent responses to a separate thinking file, sorted by timestamp."""
    log_dir = Path("Logs/Architect/Session")
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Find existing session file to match naming convention
    session_name = session_id.title() if session_id else "Unknown"
    md_files = list(log_dir.glob(f"Architect_*_{session_name}.md"))
    
    if not md_files:
        print(f"WARNING: No session log file found for: {session_name}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available files in {log_dir}:", file=sys.stderr)
        for file in log_dir.glob("*.md"):
            print(f"  - {file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    # Use the most recent session file to get the naming pattern
    session_file = max(md_files, key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime)
    print(f"Found session file: {session_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Create thinking file with matching naming convention (avoid double "Thinking")
    if "Architect_Thinking_" in session_file.name:
        # File already has Thinking prefix, use it as-is
        thinking_file = session_file
    else:
        # Replace only the first occurrence to avoid duplication
        thinking_file = session_file.parent / session_file.name.replace("Architect_", "Architect_Thinking_", 1)
    
    print(f"Target thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Delete existing thinking file if it exists
    if thinking_file.exists():
        print(f"Deleting existing thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        thinking_file.unlink()
    
    # Sort agent responses by timestamp
    sorted_responses = sorted(agent_responses, key=lambda x: x.get('timestamp', ''))
    
    try:
        # Create new thinking file with header
        with open(thinking_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f"# Agent Thinking - {session_name}\n")
            f.write(f"**Session ID**: {session_id}\n")
            f.write(f"**Generated**: {datetime.now().isoformat()}\n")
            f.write(f"**Total Responses**: {len(sorted_responses)}\n")
            f.write("---\n\n")
            
            for response in sorted_responses:
                f.write(format_agent_response(response))
        
        print(f"Successfully created thinking file: {thinking_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to write thinking file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)


def main() -> None:
    """Main function to extract and log agent responses."""
    print("Agent response extractor started", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Read session_id from stdin hook data
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
        print(f"Received hook data: {list(data.keys())}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: Failed to parse stdin JSON: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    session_id = data.get("session_id", "unknown")
    print(f"Session ID: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Find transcript file
    transcript_dir = Path(os.path.expandvars("%APPDATA%\\devin\\cli\\transcripts"))
    transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
    print(f"Looking for transcript: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Fallback to Linux/Mac path
    if not transcript_file.exists():
        transcript_dir = Path.home() / ".local/share/devin/cli/transcripts"
        transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        print(f"Fallback path: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    if not transcript_file.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: Transcript file not found: {transcript_file}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available transcripts:", file=sys.stderr)
        try:
            for file in transcript_dir.glob("*.json"):
                print(f"  - {file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        except:
            pass
        return
    
    print(f"Extracting agent responses from transcript: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Extract agent responses
    agent_responses = extract_agent_responses(transcript_file)
    
    if not agent_responses:
        print(f"No agent responses found in transcript", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    
    print(f"Found {len(agent_responses)} agent responses", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Write to separate thinking file
    write_thinking_file(session_id, agent_responses)

"""Agent response extractor - extracts agent text responses from transcript files."""

import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> None:
    """Main function to extract and log agent responses."""
    try:
        # Read session_id from stdin hook data
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
        session_id = data.get("session_id", "unknown")
        
        # Find transcript file
        transcript_dir = Path(os.path.expandvars("%APPDATA%\\devin\\cli\\transcripts"))
        transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        
        # Fallback to Linux/Mac path
        if not transcript_file.exists():
            transcript_dir = Path.home() / ".local/share/devin/cli/transcripts"
            transcript_file = transcript_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        
        if not transcript_file.exists():
            print(f"Transcript not found: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        
        # Extract agent responses
        with open(transcript_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            transcript = json.load(f)
        
        agent_responses = []
        steps = transcript.get('steps', [])
        for step in steps:
            if step.get('source') == 'agent':
                reasoning = step.get('reasoning_content', '').strip()
                message = step.get('message', '').strip()
                if reasoning or message:
                    agent_responses.append(step)
        
        if not agent_responses:
            print(f"No agent responses found: {session_id}", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        
        # Find session file
        log_dir = Path("Logs/Architect/Session")
        session_name = session_id.title() if session_id else "Unknown"
        md_files = list(log_dir.glob(f"Architect_*_{session_name}.md"))
        
        if not md_files:
            print(f"No session file found: {session_name}", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        
        session_file = max(md_files, key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime)
        thinking_file = session_file.parent / session_file.name.replace("Architect_", "Architect_Thinking_", 1)
        
        # Sort and write
        sorted_responses = sorted(agent_responses, key=lambda x: x.get('timestamp', ''))
        
        with open(thinking_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f"# Agent Thinking - {session_name}\n")
            f.write(f"**Session ID**: {session_id}\n")
            f.write(f"**Generated**: {datetime.now().isoformat()}\n")
            f.write(f"**Total Responses**: {len(sorted_responses)}\n")
            f.write("---\n\n")
            
            for response in sorted_responses:
                timestamp = response.get('timestamp', '')
                step_id = response.get('step_id', 'unknown')
                model = response.get('model_name', 'unknown')
                reasoning = response.get('reasoning_content', '')
                message = response.get('message', '')
                
                f.write(f"### AGENT_RESPONSE\n")
                f.write(f"**Timestamp**: {timestamp}\n")
                f.write(f"**Step ID**: {step_id}\n")
                f.write(f"**Model**: {model}\n")
                f.write("\n")
                
                full_response = ""
                if reasoning:
                    full_response += reasoning
                if message:
                    if full_response:
                        full_response += "\n\n" + message
                    else:
                        full_response = message
                
                if full_response:
                    f.write("**Response**:\n")
                    f.write("```\n")
                    f.write(full_response)
                    f.write("\n```\n")
                else:
                    f.write("**Response**: [empty]\n")
                
                f.write("\n---\n\n")
        
        print(f"Created thinking file: {thinking_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def format_readable_entry(entry: dict) -> str:
    """Format a log entry for maximum readability with markdown formatting."""
    formatted = []
    
    # Header with markdown
    formatted.append(f"### {entry.get('event', 'unknown').upper()}")
    formatted.append(f"**Timestamp**: {entry.get('timestamp', 'unknown')}")
    formatted.append(f"**Session**: {entry.get('session_id', 'unknown')}")
    
    if 'prompt_id' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Prompt ID**: {entry['prompt_id']}")
    
    if 'agent' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Agent**: {entry['agent']}")
    
    if 'working_directory' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Working Directory**: {entry['working_directory']}")
    
    formatted.append("")  # Empty line for separation
    
    # Prompt content with markdown
    if 'prompt' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Prompt**:")
        formatted.append("```")
        formatted.append(str(entry['prompt']))
        formatted.append("```")
        formatted.append("")
    
    formatted.append("---")
    formatted.append("")
    
    return "\n".join(formatted)

def format_readable_entry(entry: dict) -> str:
    """Format a log entry for maximum readability with markdown formatting."""
    formatted = []
    
    # Header with markdown
    formatted.append(f"### {entry.get('event', 'unknown').upper()}")
    formatted.append(f"**Timestamp**: {entry.get('timestamp', 'unknown')}")
    formatted.append(f"**Session**: {entry.get('session_id', 'unknown')}")
    
    if 'prompt_id' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Prompt ID**: {entry['prompt_id']}")
    
    if 'agent' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Agent**: {entry['agent']}")
    
    if 'working_directory' in entry:
        formatted.append(f"**Working Directory**: {entry['working_directory']}")
    
    formatted.append("")  # Empty line for separation
    
    # Prompt content with markdown

        formatted.append(f"**Prompt**:")
        formatted.append("```")
        formatted.append(str(entry['prompt']))
        formatted.append("```")

## 4. feat(hooks): add Devin CLI integration
URL: https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/pull/3144

- `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` â€” `run_devin()` / `process_devin_payload()` / `devin_response_from_decision()`. Emits the Devin PreToolUse JSON response (`decision` + `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput.command`). If a command is allowed but RTK has no filter for it, the original command is approved unchanged.
...
Devin CLI exposes a documented `PreToolUse` hook that fires before the `exec` tool runs:
...
The hook can return:
...
- `decision: approve/block` to control execution
- `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput` to rewrite tool arguments before execution
...
- Matcher `^exec$` because Devin routes shell commands through the `exec` tool.
- Read `permissions` from Devin's own config files so users do not maintain a second allowlist; `Exec(git status)` in Devin `allow` maps to RTK's `allow` rule for `git status`.
- Support `hooks.v1.json` (root event map) and `config.json`/`config.local.json` (nested under `hooks`) because Devin CLI reads hooks from all of these locations.
- Respect `$DEVIN_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and `%APPDATA%` for global config resolution.
- Approve the original command unchanged when RTK has no filter but the user explicitly allowed it, preserving Devin CLI Normal/Bypass/Autonomous mode semantics.
...
Hook responses:
...
```bash

{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"command":"rtk git status"}},"decision":"approve"}

{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"command":"rtk git branch -a"}}}

$ echo '{"tool_name":"exec","tool_input":{"command":"python3 -c \"print(1)\""}}' | rtk hook devin
{"decision":"approve"}

import sys

def main():
    """Block redundant edits to save tokens."""
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:

    tool_input = data.get("tool_input", {})
    
    # Only check edit operations
    if tool_name != "edit":
        sys.exit(0)  # Allow non-edit tools
    
    old_string = tool_input.get("old_string", "")
    new_string = tool_input.get("new_string", "")
    
    # Block if strings are identical
    if old_string == new_string:
        print("Blocked redundant edit: old_string == new_string", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)  # Block the edit
    
    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the edit

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## 3. overview
URL: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview

Hooks are configured with a JSON format. Place them in your project's `.devin/` directory (or a user-level config) and Devin CLI runs them at the matching lifecycle events. Existing hooks in `.claude/` directories are also picked up automatically â€” see [Where Hooks Live](#where-hooks-live).
...
Create `.devin/hooks.v1.json` in your project:
...
```json theme={null}
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/check-command.sh"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
...
This runs `./scripts/check-command.sh` before every shell command execution. The script receives event data on stdin and can block the action by returning a non-zero exit code.
...
| Event | When it fires |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool finishes |
| `PermissionRequest` | When a permission decision is needed |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | When the user submits a message |
| `Stop` | When the agent wants to stop |
| `SessionStart` | When a session begins |
| `SessionEnd` | When a session ends |
...
Each hook has a **type** (`command` or `prompt`), an optional **matcher** (regex on the hook event's `tool_name`), and configuration:
...
```json theme={null}
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/validate.sh",
          "timeout": 10
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
...
| Field | Description |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `matcher` | Regex matched against the hook event's `tool_name`. Empty string or an omitted matcher matches all tool names. |
| `type` | `"command"` to run a shell command, or `"prompt"` to evaluate an LLM prompt. |
| `command` | Shell command to run (for `command` type). |
| `prompt` | LLM prompt to evaluate (f...

## 4. Medium
URL: https://ai.sulat.com/devin-cli-beyond-the-defaults-3487abea6596

Hooks run shell commands or LLM prompts at specific points in the agentâ€™s lifecycle. They are the policy enforcement layer: block destructive commands, inject context before tool calls, log what the agent does, auto-approve safe operations without switching to Bypass mode.
...
The hook format is compatible with Claude Code hooks, so any hooks you already have written will work here.
...
Create`.devin/hooks.v1.json` at your project root. The file structure is the hook event name as the top-level key:
...
```
{  "PreToolUse": [    {      "matcher": "exec",      "hooks": [        {          "type": "command",          "command": "./scripts/check-command.sh"        }      ]    }  ]}
```
...
This runs`check-command.sh` before every shell command. The script receives the event data on stdin as JSON:
...
```
{  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",  "tool_name": "exec",  "tool_input": {    "command": "rm -rf /tmp/build"  }}
```
...
Exit code 2 is the most important number youâ€™ll need to remember for agentic harnesses. Configured correctly, hooks prevent bad code from reaching production.
...
To return a reason to the agent, write JSON to stdout:
...
```
{  "decision": "block",  "reason": "Destructive command blocked by policy"}
...
The matcher field is a regex, not a glob.`"exec"` matches any tool name containing "exec".`"^exec$"` matches only the exact`exec` tool. For MCP tools, use`"^mcp__github__.*"` to match all tools on the`github` server.
...
Practical hook examples:
...
Block`rm -rf` in one line:
...
```
{  "PreToolUse": [    {      "matcher": "exec",      "hooks": [        {          "type": "command",          "command": "python3 -c \"import sys, json; data = json.load(sys.stdin); cmd = data.get('tool_input', {}).get('command', ''); sys.exit(2 if 'rm -rf' in cmd else 0)\""        }      ]    }  ]}
```
...

...
```
{  "PermissionRequest": [    {      "matcher": "exec",      "hooks": [        {          "type": "command",...

URL: https://cognitionai.mintlify.app/cli/extensibility/hooks/lifecycle-hooks

## PreToolUse
...
Fires before a tool executes. Use this to block, modify, or add context to tool calls.
...
| Field | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_name` | Name of the tool being called | `exec`, `edit`, `mcp__github__create_issue` |
| `tool_input` | Arguments passed to the tool | `{ "command": "rm -rf /", "shell_id": "main" }` |
...
Example â€” Block destructive commands:
...
```json
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "exec",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "python3 -c \"import sys, json; data = json.load(sys.stdin); cmd = data.get('tool_input', {}).get('command', ''); sys.exit(2 if 'rm -rf' in cmd else 0)\""
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
...
Example â€” Require confirmation for writes outside src/:
...
Use a script that inspects the tool input and returns a decision:
...
```json
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "edit",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./scripts/check-edit-path.sh",
          "timeout": 5
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

```

...
```json
{

    "updatedInput": {

## 1. [Docs] Clarify behavior and precedence of advanced JSON output fields for Hooks Â· Issue #6966 Â· anthropics/claude-code
URL: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6966

A critical point of confusion is the distinction between stopping a single tool call versus stopping the entire agent loop.
...
For example, for a `PreToolUse` hook, the outcomes of these two payloads are vastly different:
...
```json
    {
      "permissionDecision": "deny",
      "permissionDecisionReason": "Tool not allowed for this file type."
    }
    ```
 * **Actual Outcome:** Blocks the *current tool call*, feeds the reason back to Claude, and allows the agent to replan and attempt a different action.
...
1. **Payload to terminate the agent loop:**
...
```json
    {
      "continue": false,
      "stopReason": "Aborting agent due to security policy violation."
    }
    ```
 * **Actual Outcome:** Terminates the *entire agent loop* for the current task, stopping all further action from Claude.
...
| Field | Applies To (Events) | Effect | Key Distinction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `permissionDecision: "deny"` | `PreToolUse` | **Blocks a single tool call.** The agent is informed and can try an alternative. | Agent continues, but this specific action is prevented. |
...
| `decision: "block"` | `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, etc. | **Feeds an error back to the agent.** The agent must respond to the feedback. | The agent is forced to react to the hook's feedback. |
...
| `continue: false` | All Events | **Terminates the entire agent loop.** The session stops processing the current task. | Agent stops completely. This is a hard stop, not a course correction. |
...
* How to block just one tool call (using `permissionDecision`).
 * How to stop the entire agent (using `continue: false`).
 * How to give feedback to the agent after a tool has run (using `decision: "block"`).
...
* "If a hook's JSON output includes `continue: false`, it will always terminate the agent loop, regardless of other fields like `permissionDecision`."
 * "For `PreToolUse` hooks, `permissionDecision` takes precedence over the deprecated `decision` field."
...

## 2. 05.4%20Hooks.md at main Â· Vizzuality/claude-code-vault
URL: https://github.com/Vizzuality/claude-code-vault/blob/main/05.4%20Hooks.md

Hooks are event listeners on the agent loop. They run your code at
specific points in the loop: before a tool executes, after it executes,
when the model decides to stop, when a session starts or ends, and more.
...
```
while True:
 response = call_api(system, messages, tools)
 messages.append(response)

 tool_calls = extract_tool_calls(response)
 if not tool_calls:
 break # <-- Stop event fires here

 for call in tool_calls:
 # <-- PreToolUse fires here
 result = execute_tool(call)
 # <-- PostToolUse fires here
 messages.append(result)
...
That is the mental model. Hooks do not change the API call. They do not
modify `system`, `messages`, or `tools`. They sit *between* the model's
decision and the execution of that decision. This is the same distinction
as middleware in a web framework: the request and response stay the same,
but you can inspect, approve, deny, or react to them.
...
| Event | When it fires | What you can do |
|---|---|---|
| `PreToolUse` | After model returns tool_use, before execution | Approve, deny, or inspect |
| `PostToolUse` | After tool executes successfully | React to output |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After tool execution fails | React to errors |
| `Stop` | Model returns text with no tool calls (loop breaks) | Run final checks |
| `SubagentStart` | A sub-agent's loop begins | Inspect or configure |
| `SubagentStop` | A sub-agent's loop ends | Inspect sub-agent results |
| `SessionStart` | Session begins, before first API call | Load context, set env vars |
| `SessionEnd` | Session terminates | Cleanup, logging |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User sends a message | Transform or validate input |
|
...
PreCompact` | Before
...
compaction | Preserve information |
|
...
The two you will use most are `PreToolUse` and `Stop`. PreToolUse is
where you enforce rules ("never write to /etc", "always run tests before
committing"). Stop is where you verify the model actually finished
what it started.
...

## 3. PreToolUse hooks with preventContinuation:true are not blocking tool execution
URL: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/3514

# PreToolUse hooks with preventContinuation:true are not blocking tool execution
...
PreToolUse hooks that return `{"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."}` are not preventing tool execution despite Claude Code correctly parsing and processing the hook response with `preventContinuation: true`.
...
When a PreToolUse hook returns `{"continue": false}`, the tool should not be executed and the user should see the `stopReason` message instead.
...
The hook is executed correctly and returns the blocking response, but the tool execution continues anyway.
...
JSON output
[DEBUG] Parsed JSON output from hook: {"
...
,"stopReason":"Use ~/globalvenv/
...
python3 instead of installing packages with pip3."}
[DEBUG] Processed hook result: {"preventContinuation":true,"stopReason":"Use ~/globalvenv/bin/python3 instead of installing packages with pip3."}
...
Note the last line: despite `preventContinuation: true`, the Bash tool is still invoked.
...
1. Create a PreToolUse hook script that returns `{"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."}`
2. Configure the hook in settings for the Bash tool
3. Attempt to run a command that the hook should block
4. Observe that the tool executes despite the hook rejection
...
- The hook itself is working correctly (proper JSON response, correct exit codes)

## 4. Hooks and Lifecycle Events: Intercepting Agent Behavior - AgentPatterns.ai
URL: https://agentpatterns.ai/tool-engineering/hooks-lifecycle-events/

The model processes instructions. The shell runs hooks. Under task pressure the model may deprioritize an instruction, but a hook always runs. The runtime spawns the hook as a`PreToolUse` or`PostToolUse` subprocess before or after the model acts. It then proceeds or blocks based on the hook's exit code and JSON response. The model cannot override hook logic through reasoning.
...
| Event | When it fires | Can block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool call executes | Yes |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool call completes | No |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User sends a message | Yes (some tools) |
| `Stop` | Agent finishes a turn | No |
| `InstructionsLoaded` | CLAUDE.md or`.claude/rules/*.md` loads | No |
| `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` | Sub-agent spawns or completes | No |
...
`PreToolUse` enforces. It receives the tool name and inputs, can block the call, and returns a reason the model must adapt to.`PostToolUse` automates. It only observes, but it can trigger side effects like logging or linting.
...
`PreToolUse` blocks by returning
...
Un-matched hooks fire on every event of that type. Session-level events such as`Stop` and`UserPromptSubmit` do not support matchers.
...
| Use case | Event | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block disallowed commands | `PreToolUse`(Bash) | Deny + redirect |
| Enforce package manager | `PreToolUse`(Bash) | Match`npm`, redirect to`bun` |
| Auto-lint after edits | `PostToolUse`(Edit/Write) | Run linter |
| Audit tool calls | `PostToolUse` | Append to log |
| Notify on completion | `Stop` | Desktop notification |
| Scan for secrets | `PreToolUse`(Write) | Match content, deny if found |
...
- Hooks execute in the shell â€” the model cannot override them
- `PreToolUse` enforces;`PostToolUse` automates
- Matchers scope hooks to specific tools; session events fire unconditionally
- Project hooks in`.claude/settings.json` enforce team conventions
- `InstructionsLoaded` audits which instruction files loaded at session start
- `agent...

PreToolUse
...
The `PreToolUse` hook fires before the agent invokes a tool.
...
The `Stop` hook fires when the agent session ends. When scoped to a custom agent, the `Stop` hook is also treated as `SubagentStop`.
...
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `stop_hook_active` | boolean | `true` when the agent is already continuing as a result of a previous stop hook. Check this value to prevent the agent from running indefinitely. |
...
### Stop output
...
The `Stop` hook can prevent the agent from stopping:
...
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "Stop",
    "decision": "block",
    "reason": "Run the test suite before finishing"
  }
}
...
| Field | Values | Description |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| `decision` | `"block"` | Prevent the agent from stopping |
| `reason` | string | Required when decision is `"block"`. Tells the agent why it should continue. |
...
> [!IMPORTANT]
> When a `Stop` hook blocks the agent from stopping, the agent continues running and the additional turns consume [AI credits](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/conâ€¦ (141 chars truncated)

**New String** (1854 chars):

## Exit Codes and JSON Responses

Hook exit codes and JSON responses control behavior:

### Exit Codes

|| Code | Meaning |
||------|---------|
|| 0 | Success â€” hook continues normally |
|| 2 | Block â€” action is denied (may stop entire agent loop) |
|| Other | Error â€” logged but doesn't block |

### JSON Response Format (Recommended)

For proper workflow gating, use JSON responses instead of exit codes:

**Block single tool call without stopping agent:**
```json
{
  "permissionDecision": "deny",
  "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
}
```

**Key distinction:**
- `permissionDecision: "deny"` â†’ Blocks a **single tool call**, agent can continue and try other actions
- Exit code 2 â†’ May be interpreted as a hard stop that terminates the entire agent loop
- `continue: false` â†’ Terminates the entire agent loop completely

**Example implementation:**
```python
import json
import sys

def main():
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:
        sys.exit(0)
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = data.get("tool_input", {})
    
    # Block redundant edits
    if tool_name == "edit":
        old_string = tool_input.get("old_string", "")
        new_string = tool_input.get("new_string", "")
        
        if old_string == new_string:
            response = {
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
            }
            print(json.dumps(response))
            sys.exit(0)  # Return success with JSON response
    
    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the action

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**Important:** When using JSON responses, always exit with code 0. The blocking decision is communicated through the JSON payload, not the exit code.
```

    "new_string": "## Exit Codes and JSON Responses\n\nHook exit codes and JSON responses control behavior:\n\n### Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success \u00e2\u20ac\u201d hook continues normally |\n| 2 | Block \u00e2\u20ac\u201d action is denied (may stop entire agent loop) |\n| Other | Error \u00e2\u20ac\u201d logged but doesn't block |\n\n### JSON Response Format (Recommended)\n\nFor proper workflow gating, use JSON responses instead of exit codes:\n\n**Block single tool call without stopping agent:**\n```json\n{\n  \"permissionDecision\": \"deny\",\n  \"permissionDecisionReason\": \"Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string\"\n}\n```\n\n**Key distinction:**\n- `permissionDecision: \"deny\"` \u00e2\u2020\u2019 Blocks a **single tool call**, agent can continue and try other actions\n- Exit code 2 \u00e2\u2020\u2019 May be interpreted as a hard stop that terminates the entire agent loop\n- `continue: false` \u00e2\u2020\u2019 Terminates the entire agent loop completely\n\n**Example implementation:**\n```python\nimport json\nimport sys\n\ndef main():\n    try:\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except:\n        sys.exit(0)\n    \n    tool_name = data.get(\"tool_name\", \"\")\n    tool_input = data.get(\"tool_input\", {})\n    \n    # Block redundant edits\n    if tool_name == \"edit\":\n        old_string = tool_input.get(\"old_string\", \"\")\n        new_string = tool_input.get(\"new_string\", \"\")\n        \n        if old_string == new_string:\n            response = {\n                \"permissionDecision\": \"deny\",\n                \"permissionDecisionReason\": \"Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string\"\n            }\n            print(json.dumps(response))\n            sys.exit(0)  # Return success with JSON response\n    \n    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the action\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n**Important:** When using JSON responses, always exit with code 0. The blocking decision is communicated through the JSON payload, not the exit code."

import json
import sys

def main():
    """Block redundant edits to save tokens."""
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception as e:
        sys.exit(0)  # Allow if we can't parse
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = data.get("tool_input", {})
    
    # Only check edit operations

        sys.exit(0)  # Allow non-edit tools
    
    old_string = tool_input.get("old_string", "")
    new_string = tool_input.get("new_string", "")
    
    # Block if strings are identical
    if old_string == new_string:
        # Return JSON response to block single tool call without stopping agent
        response = {
            "permissionDecision": "deny",
            "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
        }
        print(json.dumps(response))
        sys.exit(0)  # Return success with JSON response
    
    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the edit

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

 Block dangerous commands, require confirmation for specific actions, or restrict file access.

 Execute scripts, send notifications, or log events when things happen.
 

 
 Dynamically grant or restrict permissions based on the situation.

## 4. feat(hooks): add Devin CLI integration
URL: https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/pull/3144

Adds first-class [Devin CLI](https://docs.devin.ai/cli) support to RTK, following the same hook/rewrite pattern already used for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and Factory Droid.
...
- `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` â€” `run_devin()` / `process_devin_payload()` / `devin_response_from_decision()`. Emits the Devin PreToolUse JSON response (`decision` + `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput.command`). If a command is allowed but RTK has no filter for it, the original command is approved unchanged.
...
Devin CLI exposes a documented `PreToolUse` hook that fires before the `exec` tool runs:
...
project config precedence
...
ai/cli/
...
/global-vs-local)
...
The hook can return:
...
- `decision: approve/block` to control execution
- `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput` to rewrite tool arguments before execution
...
This is the same shape RTK already uses for Claude Code and Cursor, so a Devin integration fits the existing architecture without adding new dependencies.
...
- Matcher `^exec$` because Devin routes shell commands through the `exec` tool.
- Read `permissions` from Devin's own config files so users do not maintain a second allowlist; `Exec(git status)` in Devin `allow` maps to RTK's `allow` rule for `git status`.
- Support `hooks.v1.json` (root event map) and `config.json`/`config.local.json` (nested under `hooks`) because Devin CLI reads hooks from all of these locations.
- Respect `$DEVIN_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and `%APPDATA%` for global config resolution.
- Approve the original command unchanged when RTK has no filter but the user explicitly allowed it, preserving Devin CLI Normal/Bypass/Autonomous mode semantics.
...
Hook responses:

## [BUG] PreToolUse hook exit code 2 causes Claude to stop instead of acting on error feedback
...
When a `PreToolUse` hook blocks a tool call by exiting with code 2, Claude stops responding and waits for user input instead of acting on the error feedback provided via stderr.
...
Per the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event), exit code 2 on `PreToolUse` "blocks the tool call" and "stderr text is fed back to Claude as an error message." The expected behavior is that Claude receives the error message and can reason about it â€” for example, fixing lint errors and retrying a commit. Instead, Claude treats the blocked tool call as a full stop and goes idle, requiring the user to manually type "continue" or similar to resume.
...
This behavior is **intermittent** â€” sometimes Claude does act on the feedback correctly, but increasingly it stops. The inconsistency suggests the model is interpreting the "blocked tool call" signal as a reason to defer to the user, rather than as actionable feedback.
...
The stderr output includes explicit directives telling Claude to continue:
...

...

...

2. Run: git add -v .
3. Retry the exact same commit command
...
Do NOT stop, do NOT end your turn, do NOT ask the user to continue.
</claude-directive>
...
```
**PreToolUse hook blocks are automated quality checks, NOT user denials.**

Critical directives:
- Do NOT ask the user for permission to fix lint/format errors â€” fix them autonomously
- Do NOT stop or end your turn when a commit is blocked by a hook
- Do NOT treat a hook block as a user denial â€” it is a machine-generated quality gate

## Exit Codes and JSON Responses

Hook exit codes and JSON responses control behavior:

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Success â€” hook continues normally |
| 2 | Block â€” action is denied (may stop entire agent loop) |
| Other | Error â€” logged but doesn't block |

### JSON Response Format (Recommended)

For proper workflow gating, use JSON responses instead of exit codes:

**Block single tool call without stopping agent:**
```json
{
  "permissionDecision": "deny",
  "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
}
```

**Key distinction:**
- `permissionDecision: "deny"` â†’ Blocks a **single tool call**, agent can continue and try other actions
- Exit code 2 â†’ May be interpreted as a hard stop that terminates the entire agent loop
- `continue: false` â†’ Terminates the entire agent loop completely

**Example implementation:**
```python
import json
import sys

def main():
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:
        sys.exit(0)
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = data.get("tool_input", {})
    
    # Block redundant edits
    if tool_name == "edit":
        old_string = tool_input.get("old_string", "")
        new_string = tool_input.get("new_string", "")
        
        if old_string == new_string:
            response = {
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
            }
            print(json.dumps(response))
            sys.exit(0)  # Return success with JSON response
    
    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the action

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**Important:** When using JSON responses, always exit with code 0. The blocking decision is communicated through the JSON payload, not the exit code.
```

## Exit Codes and Blocking Behavior

**IMPORTANT KNOWN ISSUE**: PreToolUse hooks that block tool calls often cause the agent to stop completely rather than continue working, even though the documentation suggests they should adapt and continue.

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Success â€” hook continues normally |
| 2 | Block â€” action is denied (often stops agent workflow) |
| Other | Error â€” logged but doesn't block |

### Current Behavior vs Expected Behavior

**Exit Code 2 Reality:**
- **Expected**: Agent receives error feedback via stderr, can reason about it, and continues working
- **Actual**: Agent often treats blocked tool call as a full stop and goes idle, requiring user input to resume
- **Issue**: This is a known intermittent issue (Claude Code issue #24327, affects Devin CLI similarly)

**Practical Implications:**
- Blocking hooks are best used for hard security boundaries, not soft workflow guidance
- If you need the agent to continue after blocking, consider PostToolUse for logging/notification instead
- The `permissionDecision: "deny"` JSON format has similar issues with agent stopping

### JSON Response Format

**Block single tool call:**
```json
{
  "permissionDecision": "deny",
  "permissionDecisionReason": "Action blocked by policy"
}
```

**Note**: While JSON responses are documented to allow agent continuation, in practice they often cause the agent to stop similarly to exit code 2.

### Recommended Approach

For workflow gating where you want the agent to continue:
1. **Use PostToolUse** for logging and side effects instead of PreToolUse blocking
2. **Use PreToolUse only for hard security boundaries** where stopping is acceptable
3. **Provide clear guidance** in your hook output to help the agent understand what to do if it does continue

**Example of PostToolUse for workflow tracking:**
```python
import json
import sys

def main():
    """Log tool usage without blocking."""
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:
        sys.exit(0)
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    # Log the tool action
    print(f"Tool {tool_name} executed", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(0)  # Always allow

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
```

## Exit Codes and JSON Responses

Hook exit codes and JSON responses control behavior:

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Success â€” hook continues normally |
| 2 | Block â€” action is denied (may stop entire agent loop) |
| Other | Error â€” logged but doesn't block |

### JSON Response Format (Recommended)

For proper workflow gating, use JSON responses instead of exit codes:

**Block single tool call without stopping agent:**
```json
{
  "permissionDecision": "deny",
  "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
}
```

**Key distinction:**
- `permissionDecision: "deny"` â†’ Blocks a **single tool call**, agent can continue and try other actions
- Exit code 2 â†’ May be interpreted as a hard stop that terminates the entire agent loop
- `continue: false` â†’ Terminates the entire agent loop completely

**Example implementation:**
```python
import json
import sys

def main():
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:
        sys.exit(0)
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = data.get("tool_input", {})
    
    # Block redundant edits
    if tool_name == "edit":
        old_string = tool_input.get("old_string", "")
        new_string = tool_input.get("new_string", "")
        
        if old_string == new_string:
            response = {
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": "Redundant edit blocked: old_string == new_string"
            }
            print(json.dumps(response))
            sys.exit(0)  # Return success with JSON response
    
    sys.exit(0)  # Allow the action

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**Important:** When using JSON responses, always exit with code 0. The blocking decision is communicated through the JSON payload, not the exit code.

## Exit Codes and Blocking Behavior

**IMPORTANT KNOWN ISSUE**: PreToolUse hooks that block tool calls often cause the agent to stop completely rather than continue working, even though the documentation suggests they should adapt and continue.

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Success â€” hook continues normally |
| 2 | Block â€” action is denied (often stops agent workflow) |
| Other | Error â€” logged but doesn't block |

### Current Behavior vs Expected Behavior

**Exit Code 2 Reality:**
- **Expected**: Agent receives error feedback via stderr, can reason about it, and continues working
- **Actual**: Agent often treats blocked tool call as a full stop and goes idle, requiring user input to resume
- **Issue**: This is a known intermittent issue (Claude Code issue #24327, affects Devin CLI similarly)

**Practical Implications:**
- Blocking hooks are best used for hard security boundaries, not soft workflow guidance
- If you need the agent to continue after blocking, consider PostToolUse for logging/notification instead
- The `permissionDecision: "deny"` JSON format has similar issues with agent stopping

### JSON Response Format

**Block single tool call:**
```json
{
  "permissionDecision": "deny",
  "permissionDecisionReason": "Action blocked by policy"
}
```

**Note**: While JSON responses are documented to allow agent continuation, in practice they often cause the agent to stop similarly to exit code 2.

### Recommended Approach

For workflow gating where you want the agent to continue:
1. **Use PostToolUse** for logging and side effects instead of PreToolUse blocking
2. **Use PreToolUse only for hard security boundaries** where stopping is acceptable
3. **Provide clear guidance** in your hook output to help the agent understand what to do if it does continue

**Example of PostToolUse for workflow tracking:**
```python
import json
import sys

def main():
    """Log tool usage without blocking."""
    try:
        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except:
        sys.exit(0)
    
    tool_name = data.get("tool_name", "")
    # Log the tool action
    print(f"Tool {tool_name} executed", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(0)  # Always allow

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
```

## Using the Matcher
...
The `matcher` field is a **regex** matched against the hook event's `tool_name`. It is available for tool-related events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `PermissionRequest`.
...
For non-tool events (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PostCompaction`, `SessionStart`, and `SessionEnd`), there is no `tool_name`; use `""` or omit the matcher to run the hook for every event of that type.

 
 The matcher is not a permission glob. Patterns like `mcp__github__*` are useful in permissions, but hook matchers are regexes. Use `mcp__github__.*` in a hook matcher.
 

| Matcher | Matches |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `""` (empty) or omitted | All tool names for tool events |
| `"exec"` | Tool names containing `exec` |
| `"^exec$"` | Only the `exec` tool |
| `"^(exec\|edit)$"` | Only `exec` or `edit` |
| `"^mcp__.*"` | All MCP tools |
| `"^mcp__github__.*"` | All tools from the `github` MCP server |
| `"^mcp__github__create_issue$"` | The `create_issue` tool from the `github` MCP se...

For the full list of hook events, see the [Hooks reference](/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle).
...
## How hooks work
...
Hook events fire at specific lifecycle points in Claude Code. When an event fires, all matching hooks run in parallel, and identical hook commands are automatically deduplicated. The table below shows each event and when it triggers:
...
| Event | When it fires |
| :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionStart` | When a session begins or resumes |
| `Setup` | When you start Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in `-p` mode. For one-time preparation in CI or scripts |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | When you submit a prompt, before Claude processes it |
| `UserPromptExpansion` | When a user-typed command expands into a prompt, before it reaches Claude. Can block the expansion |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool call executes. Can block it |
| `PermissionRequest` | When a permission dialog appears |
| `PermissionDenied` | When a tool call is denied by the auto mode classifier. Return `{retry: true}` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call...

## 3. features-overview
URL: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview

 A hook fires on a lifecycle event; a skill is loaded into context for Claude to apply.

 | Aspect | Hook | Skill |
 | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | **Runs** | A shell command, HTTP request, LLM prompt, or subagent | Instructions Claude reads and follows |
 | **Triggered by** | [Lifecycle events](/docs/en/hooks#hook-events) such as `PostToolUse` or `SessionStart` | You typing `/ `, or Claude matching the description to your task |
 | **Determinism** | Always fires on its event; the trigger is guaranteed | Claude interprets the instructions; outcome can vary |
 | **Context cost** | Zero unless the hook returns output | Description loads each session; full content loads when used |
 | **Best for** | Linting after edits, blocking unsafe commands, logging, notifications | Workflows that need reasoning, reference material, multi-step tasks |

 **Use a hook** when the action must happen the same way every time and doesn't need Claude to think. For example: format on save, reject `rm -rf /`, post a Slack message when a session ends.

 **Use a skill** when Claude should decide how to apply the steps, or when the content is knowledge rather than a script. For example: a `/release` checklist, your API style guide, a debugging playbook.

 **Put guardrails in hooks.** An instruction like "never edit `.env`" in CLAUDE.md or a skill is a request, not a guarantee. A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks the edit is enforcement. If a rule must hold every time, make it a hook rather than...
